This is an online E log book to discuss our patient's de-identified health data shared after taking his\/her\/guardian's signed informed consent.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHere we discuss our individual patient's problems through series of inputs from available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patient's clinical problems with collective current best evidence based inputs.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis E log book also reflects my patient-centered online learning portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment box is welcome.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHere is a case i have seen:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003ECASE DISCUSSION\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E63 year old female came with complaints of fever since 5 days and headache since 5 days\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EHISTORY OF PRESENTING ILLNESS\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient was apparently asymptomatic 5 days back when she developed fever with headache , fever was low grade , intermittent in nature and increased at night\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHeadache was continuous in parietal region non radiating, without any aggrevating , relieving factors ( no medication )\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo h\/o vomitings, loose stools,blood in stools, rash, sore throat, cough,\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EPast History\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4 months ago patient complained of fever , taken to nalgonda government hospital where she was diagnosed with anemia and thrombocytopenia. text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u0026nbsp;This is an online E log book to discuss our patient's de-identified health data shared after taking his\/her\/guardian's signed informed consent.\u0026nbsp;\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHere we discuss our individual patient's problems through series of inputs from available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patient's clinical problems with collective current best evidence based inputs.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis E log book also reflects my patient-centered online learning portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment box is welcome.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHere is a case i have seen:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cu\u003E\u003Cb\u003ECASE DISCUSSION\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA 56 year old female patient came to the op with complaints of shortness of breath since 2 months\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EHISTORY OF PRESENTING ILLNESS\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient was apparently alright 2months ago then she developed Shortness of Breath which was insidious in onset , aggravated on exertion like walking . Relieved on taking rest , associated with seasonal variation , not associated with diurnal variation .\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo orthopnea , pedal edema , Paroxysmal nocturnal dispneoa , decreased urine output .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo h\/o fever , vomitings, loose stools , sore throat , chest pain , palpitations , blurring of vision\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe is a k\/c\/o HTN since 9years\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EK\/c\/o Asthma since 10years and on Formeterol\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EK\/c\/o CVA (Acute infarct in left semi ovale ) 1 year back\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe is a k\/c\/o psychiatric disorder in which she talks to herself and laughs at herself and she is on Amisulpride\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EON EXAMINATION\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPt is Concious, Coherent, co-operative\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo Pallor , Icterus , Clubbing, Cyanosis Lymphadenopathy, pedal oedema\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EVITALS:\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;Temp: Afebrile\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPulse : 85\/min irregularly irregular\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EResp rate : 22\/min\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBp: 150\/90 mm hg\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003ESYSTEMIC EXAMINATION\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECVS : S1,S2 heard ,no murmurs\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECNS : No focal neurological deficits\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERS: decreased air entry on right side\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPA: soft, non tender\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; Neue\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Segoe UI\u0026quot;, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, \u0026quot;Open Sans\u0026quot;, sans-serif\"\u003EThis occurs at the level of the sphincter of Oddi, a round muscle located at the opening of the bile duct into the small intestine. If a stone from the gallbladder should travel down the common bile duct and get stuck at the sphincter, it blocks outflow of all material from the liver and pancreas. This results in inflammation of the pancreas that can be quite severe.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2)sob- acidosis due to renal failure\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;? background-clip: initial; background-image: initial; background-origin: initial; background-position: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-size: initial; color: #2196f3; text-decoration-line: none;\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/link.springer.com\/article\/10.1007\/s00534-005-1050-8\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1)fluid replacement\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIncreased vascular permeability in acute pancreatitis causes the loss of intravenous fluid and reduces plasma volume. In severe cases, in patients with massive ascites, pleural effusion, and retroperitoneal and mesenteric edema, circulating plasma volume decreases markedly. Hypovolemia may lead to shock and acute renal failure, and, because hypovolemic shock may impair the pancreatic microcirculation and promote pancreatic ischemia and necrosis, restoration and maintenance of plasma volume is crucial in severe acute pancreatitis.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2) antibiotics\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOn the other hand, a placebo-controlled, double-blind trial of ciprofloxacin\u0026nbsp; +\u0026nbsp; metronidazole in patients with predicted severe acute pancreatitis showed that prophylactic administration of these antibiotics did not prevent pancreatic infection (Level 1b).\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3)analgesics\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4) nebulization in view of b\/l wheeze secondary to ?copd\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E5)diuretics for decreased urine output due to renal failure\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENon pharmacological interventions\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1)nill per mouth\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/27107634\/\" style=\"background-attachment: initial; background-clip: initial; background-image: initial; background-origin: initial; background-position: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-size: initial; color: #2196f3; text-decoration-line: none;\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/27107634\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2)ryles tube catheterisation\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3)oxygenation\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EQuestion 2:(55M)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/aakansharaj.blogspot.com\/2020\/11\/55-year-old-male-with-anemia.html?m=1\" style=\"background-attachment: initial; background-clip: initial; background-image: initial; background-origin: initial; background-position: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-size: initial; color: #2196f3; text-decoration-line: none;\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/aakansharaj.blogspot.com\/2020\/11\/55-year-old-male-with-anemia.html?m=1\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1)bone marrow and bones\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2)kidneys\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC3205153\/\" style=\"background-attachment: initial; background-clip: initial; background-image: initial; background-origin: initial; background-position: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-size: initial; color: #2196f3; text-decoration-line: none;\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC3205153\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe pathophysiology of renal failure in multiple myeloma is often multifactorial but is mostly due to the high excretion of immunoglobulin free light chains. When the light chains combine with Tamm-Horsfall proteins, they form obstructing casts (\u003Ca class=\" bibr popnode tag_hotlink tag_tooltip\" co-class=\"co-refbox\" co-rid=\"B5\" href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC3205153\/#B5\" id=\"__tag_328219526\" rid=\"B5\" style=\"background-attachment: initial; background-clip: initial; background-image: initial; background-origin: initial; background-position: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-size: initial; color: #2196f3; text-decoration-line: none;\"\u003E5\u003C\/a\u003E). Chemotherapy should therefore be initiated rapidly to decrease light chain production. Intravenous fluids can be given to treat volume depletion, hypercalcemia, or hyperuricemia.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3)lungs(infection-incrsead susceptibility)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.cancer.org\/cancer\/multiple-myeloma\/causes-risks-prevention\/what-causes.html\" style=\"background-attachment: initial; background-clip: initial; background-image: initial; background-origin: initial; background-position: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-size: initial; color: #2196f3; text-decoration-line: none;\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.cancer.org\/cancer\/multiple-myeloma\/causes-risks-prevention\/what-causes.html\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;Source Sans Pro\u0026quot;, sans-serif\"\u003EResearchers have found that patients with plasma cell tumors have important abnormalities in other bone marrow cells and that these abnormalities may also cause excess plasma cell growth. Certain cells in the bone marrow called\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cstrong\u003Edendritic cells\u003C\/strong\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;Source Sans Pro\u0026quot;, sans-serif\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;release a hormone called interleukin-6 (IL-6), which stimulates normal plasma cells to grow. Excessive production of IL-6 by these cells appears to be an important factor in development of plasma cell tumors.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;Source Sans Pro\u0026quot;, sans-serif\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;Source Sans Pro\u0026quot;, sans-serif\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; background-clip: initial; background-image: initial; background-origin: initial; background-position: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-size: initial; color: #2196f3; text-decoration-line: none;\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.intechopen.com\/books\/update-on-multiple-myeloma\/infections-in-patients-with-multiple-myeloma-in-the-era-of-novel-agents-and-stem-cell-therapies\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHowever, the infections encountered in patients with MM include: (1) bacterial infections, predominantly involving respiratory and urinary tract, caused by\u0026nbsp;\u003Cem\u003EStreptococcus pneumonia\u003C\/em\u003E,\u0026nbsp;\u003Cem\u003EStaphylococcus aureus\u003C\/em\u003E,\u0026nbsp;\u003Cem\u003EHaemophilus influenzae\u003C\/em\u003E,\u0026nbsp;\u003Cem\u003EKlebsiella pneumonia\u003C\/em\u003E,\u0026nbsp;\u003Cem\u003EEscherichia coli\u003C\/em\u003E,\u0026nbsp;\u003Cem\u003EPseudomonas aeruginosa\u003C\/em\u003E, and\u0026nbsp;\u003Cem\u003EEnterobacteriaceae\u003C\/em\u003E; (2) viral infections caused by\u0026nbsp;\u003Cem\u003Eherpes simplex virus\u003C\/em\u003E\u0026nbsp;(HSV), VZV, and\u0026nbsp;\u003Cem\u003Ecytomegalovirus\u003C\/em\u003E\u0026nbsp;(CMV); (3) fungal infections caused by\u0026nbsp;\u003Cem\u003ECandida\u003C\/em\u003E\u0026nbsp;species and\u0026nbsp;\u003Cem\u003EAspergillus\u003C\/em\u003E\u0026nbsp;species; and (4)\u0026nbsp;\u003Cem\u003EPneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia\u003C\/em\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBlood transfusion\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EB)non pharmacological\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPleural fluid analysis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EImaging -xray skull, hrct chest\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESerum electrophoresis,sputum culture\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EQuestion 3)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"http:\/\/nithishaavula.blogspot.com\/2020\/11\/51-yr-old-male-with-hfref.html?m=1\" style=\"background-attachment: initial; background-clip: initial; background-image: initial; background-origin: initial; background-position: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-size: initial; color: #2196f3; text-decoration-line: none;\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK459381\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Echronic conditions of pressure overload may lead to RVF. These include:\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003EPrimary pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and secondary pulmonary hypertension (PH) as seen in chronic-obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) or pulmonary fibrosis)\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003ECongenital heart disease (pulmonic stenosis, right ventricular outflow tract obstruction, or a systemic RV).\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003EThe following conditions result in volume overload causing RVF:\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003EValvular insufficiency (tricuspid or pulmonic)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003ECongenital heart disease with a shunt (atrial septal defect (ASD) or anomalous pulmonary venous return (APVR)).\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003EAnother important mechanism that leads to RVF is intrinsic RV myocardial disease. This includes:\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003ERV ischemia or infarct\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003EInfiltrative diseases such as amyloidosis or sarcoidosis\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003EArrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia (ARVD)\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003ECardiomyopathy\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003EMicrovascular disease.\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003ELastly, RVF may be caused by impaired filling which is seen in the following conditions:\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003EConstrictive pericarditis\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003ETricuspid stenosis\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003ESystemic vasodilatory shock\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003ECardiac tamponade\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003ESuperior vena cava syndrome\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003EHypovolemia.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; background-clip: initial; background-image: initial; background-origin: initial; background-position: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-size: initial; color: #2196f3; text-decoration-line: none;\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/heart.bmj.com\/content\/104\/5\/407\u003C\/a\u003E(meta analysis with each class of drugs)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPreload reducers\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDiuretics\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAfterload reducers-ace inhibitors\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERate controlling agents-beta blockers\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAntiepileptics for known case of epilepsy\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EInsulin for glycemic control in diabetes.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENon pharmacological interventions\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESalt and fluid restriction\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/23787719\/\" style=\"background-attachment: initial; background-clip: initial; background-image: initial; background-origin: initial; background-position: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-size: initial; color: #2196f3; text-decoration-line: none;\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/23787719\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"BlinkMacSystemFont, -apple-system, \u0026quot;Segoe UI\u0026quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, \u0026quot;Fira Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Droid Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, sans-serif\"\u003EIndividualized salt and fluid restriction can improve signs and symptoms of CHF with no negative effects on thirst, appetite, or QoL in patients with moderate to severe CHF and previous signs of fluid retention.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EQuestion 4\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1)heart(rt and left)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC5851725\/\" style=\"background-attachment: initial; background-clip: initial; background-image: initial; background-origin: initial; background-position: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-size: initial; color: #2196f3; text-decoration-line: none;\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC5851725\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EWet beriberi is one of the clinical syndromes associated with thiamine deficiency. Thiamine, in its phosphorylated form thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP), is the precursor for the cofactor of both pyruvate dehydrogenase and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, which are both key enzymes of the Krebs cycle. The Krebs cycle is an essential part of aerobic glucose metabolism. A decrease in the activity of these 2 enzymes due to thiamine deficiency may lead to the tissue accumulation of pyruvate and lactate.[\u003Ca class=\"bibr popnode tag_hotlink tag_tooltip\" co-class=\"co-refbox\" co-rid=\"R1\" href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC5851725\/#R1\" id=\"__tag_674503700\" rid=\"R1\" style=\"background-attachment: initial; background-clip: initial; background-image: initial; background-origin: initial; background-position: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-size: initial; color: #2196f3; text-decoration-line: none;\"\u003E1\u003C\/a\u003E]\u0026nbsp;Moreover, the accumulation of pyruvate and lactate decreases peripheral resistance and increases venous blood flow, increasing the cardiac preload. Increased preload and myocardial dysfunction ultimately leads to congestive heart failure.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.medindia.net\/patients\/patientinfo\/beriberi-disease.htm\" style=\"background-attachment: initial; background-clip: initial; background-image: initial; background-origin: initial; background-position: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-size: initial; color: #2196f3; text-decoration-line: none;\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.medindia.net\/patients\/patientinfo\/beriberi-disease.htm\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EOther conditions cause\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u0026nbsp;beriberi include:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli\u003EExcessive alcohol usage, which results in inadequate intake in the diet as well as prevents the body from absorbing and storing vitamin B1.\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003EGenetic beriberi, which is an inherited condition where people lose the ability to absorb thiamine from foods. Symptoms usually present during adulthood.\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003EPregnancy; pregnant women often present with vitamin B1 deficiency. Breastfeeding infants can suffer from vitamin B1 deficiency if the mother is deficient.\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003EPeople with endocrine disorders like hyperthyroidism who require extra vitamin B1.\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003EChronic liver disease, which prevents the body from absorbing sufficient vitamin B1.\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003EKidney dialysis, which leads to a loss of vitamin B1.\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003EA prolonged bout of diarrhea, which also leads to a loss of vitamin B1.\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEjZe-VpHJBrWoAsUOJq1IYtAU8Mb1Fx7DBCeqEKtFsdGVBNk0_Iq_Ed_eZL1YniKkCFVvtEF3nhsbQ20cNGWLM35IwpzAGPDyTaMd9f3kTaglnmWSj2xmnaFggEz6as4gxqEUpmamKou772\/s1600\/1605544251430803-3.png\" imageanchor=\"1\" style=\"background-attachment: initial;
